 Steven Adams (leg) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Heat. 
 Adams played Sunday but will miss the second leg of a back-to-back set for left lower leg injury management. He and Alperen Sengun started Sunday’s win over Washington in a jumbo frontcourt lineup, but the return of Fred VanVleet means Houston can play smaller with Sengun soaking up big minutes at center. 
 Steven Adams 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #12 
 Steven Adams (calf) will start Sunday’s game against the Wizards. 
 Adams is available after missing time with a calf injury suffered during the Rockets’ season opener. With Washington starting Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr, Houston (which won’t have Fred VanVleet or Marcus Smart) will counter by starting Adams alongside Alperen Şengün. According to Rockets head coach Ime Udoka, Adams will play approximately 15 minutes. Joining Adams and Şengün in the starting lineup are Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant and Jabari Smith Jr.

 HOU 
 Center 
 #12 
 Steven Adams (calf) is available for Sunday’s game against the Wizards. 
 Sidelined since the Rockets’ season opener, Adams will be available on Sunday. He should slide into his usual backup center role, especially with Clint Capela (ankle) still out. 
 Steven Adams 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #12 
 Steven Adams (calf) is probable to play against the Wizards on Sunday. 
 Adams hasn’t played since the season opener, but he is expected to return to provide Houston with some depth off the bench. With Clint Capela still sidelined, Houston has been running smaller lineups when Alperen Sengun is on the bench, so Adams’ return will be helpful. 
 Steven Adams 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #12 
 Rockets head coach Ime Udoka said he expects Steven Adams (calf) to “miss a week or two” after undergoing imaging on his calf. 
 Adams missed Saturday’s game against Atlanta and had already been ruled out for Monday’s rematch. However, it looks like he’s going to miss at least a few more games. Clint Capela filled out the backup center minutes on Saturday and should remain in that role over the next handful of games. Capela contributed two points, three rebounds and an assist in their last game against the Hawks.

 HOU 
 Center 
 #12 
 Steven Adams (calf) is out for Monday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Adams will miss a second straight game after making his season debut in Friday’s win over the Spurs. What’s concerning is that he’s still dealing with a strained right soleus, the same injury that kept him out of the opener. Clint Capela will remain the backup center.

 HOU 
 Center 
 #12 
 Steven Adams (calf) is out for Saturday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Adams played only eight minutes in Friday’s win over the Spurs. Sitting out Saturday with calf injury management, Adams doesn’t have much fantasy value at this point in his career. 
 Steven Adams 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #12 
 Steven Adams (calf) is available for Friday’s game against the Spurs. 
 A game-time call for Friday’s game, Adams is good to go for his first appearance of the season. His availability likely pushes Clint Capela out of the rotation entirely, with Capela having logged eight minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks. 
 Steven Adams 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #12 
 Steven Adams (calf) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Spurs. 
 A game-time call for Houston’s season opener, Adams did not play in Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks. Clint Capela effectively took over backup center duties, but he played just eight minutes. Rostering Capela would not be much of a gain for fantasy managers if Adams remains out on Friday. 
 Steven Adams 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #12 
 Steven Adams (calf) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Adams was seemingly on the wrong side of questionable with a calf injury and has since been ruled out for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. Adams wasn’t likely to have much of an impact on fantasy basketball anyway, but his absence will open up some bench minutes for Clint Capela behind starter Alperen Sengun.

 Thomas Sorber (knee) underwent a procedure on his right knee on Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in 6-8 weeks. 
 Sorber, who suffered a torn ACL during his lone season at Georgetown, missed the entire 2025-26 season and has yet to make his NBA debut. Late in his return-to-play process, the Thunder center developed inflammation in the patellofemoral joint of his right knee, necessitating Tuesday’s procedure. Sorber is expected to resume on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, but this does not affect fantasy basketball.
